% Question 5
% The below code is given as a starting point. K = 10; % Find Index point within Ts for the first T_o [~,L_T_o]=min(abs(T_0-T_s)); % help min, help abs MIGHT be useful!
%Pre-Allocation of space for Matrices (speeds up Matlab) Kernel_R = zeros(K,L_T_o); Kernel_I = zeros(K,L_T_o);
% Calculation of coefficient matrix % trapz was used as a way to approximate the integral % help trapz may be useful to type into your command window
n=1; for k = -K:K Kernel_R(n,:) = cos(2*pi*k*T_s(1:L_T_o)/T_0) .* Y_t(1:L_T_o) Kernel_I(n,:) = sin(2*pi*k*T_s(1:L_T_o)/T_0) .* Y_t(1:L_T_o) A_R_k(n) = (1/T_0)*trapz(Kernel_R(n,:)); % Real A_I_k(n) = (-1j/T_0)*trapz(Kernel_I(n,:)); % Imaginary A_k(n)= A_R_k(n) + A_I_k(n) n=1+n; end
% Because trapz approximation might cause our conjugate pairs to be % slightly off (leading to imaginary values in the time domain), % we can round off to 3 digits. A_k = round(A_k,3)
% Question 6 % Hint: For each frequency, there MUST be a negative frequency pair % for each value's conjugate A_k so A_k and Freqs must be the same size k=-K:K; Freqs = k/T_0;
% Question 7 % Hint: help stem might be useful to type in your command window figure; stem(Freqs, abs(A_k)); xlabel('Frequency (Hz)'); ylabel('abs of A_k');
%{ % Question 8 % Hint: help stem might be useful to type in your command window
% Question 9
% Question 10
%% Part 3 Fourier Series (Synthesis)
% Question 11
% Note: Because of rounding approximating errors in Matlab, % it might say that your reconstructed signal is imaginary even though the % magnitude of the imaginary componet is in the power of 10^-15. % Something like max(imag(ReconstructedSignal)) could be used to test if % your signal has this problem, if so, use real(ReconstructedSignal) to % remove those small imaginary rounding errors. % WARNING: IF max(imag(ReconstructedSignal)) RETURNS A VALUE LARGER THAN % 10^-10,YOUR CODE IS NOT CORRECT!
K = ??; for k = -K:K
end
